source.title: Individual animal liveweight and daily liveweight gain, and pasture herbage mass recorded in a dairy x beef grazing study comparing contrasting grazing methods: set-stocked versus cell-grazed on a temperate permanent pasture, 2018–2025
source.attribution: Rothamsted Research. Individual animal liveweight and daily liveweight gain, and pasture herbage mass recorded in a dairy x beef grazing study comparing contrasting grazing methods: set-stocked versus cell-grazed on a temperate permanent pasture, 2018–2025. DOI: 10.23637/rothamsted.00033688. CC BY 4.0.

heldOutBaseline.method: train cohorts 1–3; predict each animal-period in cohort 4 with the training-row mean DLWG
heldOutBaseline.scope: later cohorts on the same six North Wyke plots; not new-farm generalization and not a feature model

cell-grazed.warning: descriptive only; treatment is replicated at three plots per arm, so animal-period rows are not independent treatment replicates

set-stocked.warning: descriptive only; treatment is replicated at three plots per arm, so animal-period rows are not independent treatment replicates

engineValidation.reason: The study contains ADG and plot-level herbage mass, but lacks the approved USDA CPER bout-duration/velocity predictors, individual dry-matter intake, feed costs, and a confinement arm. Its pasture treatment comparison cannot validate engine.js outputs or a pasture-versus-confinement counterfactual.
